build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not picture 29: its packed bytes end on the disk where picture 30's packed bytes begin, and the unpacker reads on to the end of its 5-sector window, so these are those bytes decoded with picture 29's value table (side 3's, this snapshot's). Nothing reads them

comments.text: Picture 29's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$0025, channel 0's script at +$000E, channel 1's script at +$0015 and 0 for channels 2 and 3, which it does not use.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 2 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 5, frame 1 then 8. One pass takes 13 steps.

Channel 1's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 5 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 2 then 10, frame 3 then 5, frame 4 then 10, frame 5 then 5, frame 6 then 10. One pass takes 40 steps.

Picture 29's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $06 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 42 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 29, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1 and 2: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 17 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 8 to 10. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
Frame 2 of picture 29, named by channel 1's entry 1: empty, a run count of 0 and the $FF that ends the frame, so draw_frame_xor ($0648) changes nothing and the entry only waits.

Frame 3 of picture 29, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entry 2: a run count of 0 to start, then 15 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 125 bitmap bytes in all (1 run of a repeated byte among them), in columns 2 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 4 of picture 29, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entry 3: a run count of 0 to start, then 14 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 80 bitmap bytes in all (2 runs of a repeated byte among them), in columns 2 to 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 5 of picture 29, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entry 4: a run count of 0 to start, then 13 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 130 bitmap bytes in all (3 runs of a repeated byte among them), in columns 2 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 6 of picture 29, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entry 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 19 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 119 bitmap bytes in all (2 runs of a repeated byte among them), in columns 2 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
The last byte picture 29's own packed bytes decode to, the 1,219th byte from $CA00: the unpacker makes it from the bits left over in the stream's last byte. Nothing reads it.
